type: Post-run review by the test author; not independent human adjudication
summary: Four pre-set expectations are debatable. Treat exact expected-label match rates as descriptive rather than population accuracy. The two clear incorrect approvals and twelve unusable Celeris-1 first-pass assessments do not depend on these disputed cases.

cases.note: Both models treated stocktaking/pet-walking search terms as a current career direction and rejected software work. The prompt says keywords are not automatically a strict allowlist, but it also says not to broaden current career direction. The original apply expectation is debatable without clearer candidate intent.

Magnus explicitly detected the fictional employer name and reserved fixture.invalid URL as test-posting indicators. Its skip decision reflects fixture metadata as well as missing duties. This is a fixture artifact, not a clean measurement of uncertainty handling.

The description does not establish an identifiable current vacancy. Skipping a placeholder and requesting clarification are both defensible under different parts of the current policy. The original uncertain expectation is not uniquely correct.

The instruction explicitly excludes software development, and the vacancy includes software development even though its proportion is unspecified. Both models' skip decision is defensible; the original uncertain expectation overstated the need for clarification.
